info.desc: The Suburbs is the third studio album by Canadian indie rock band Arcade Fire, released in August 2010. Coinciding with the announcement the band released a limited edition 12-inch single containing two tracks from the album, "The Suburbs" and "Month of May". The album debuted at No. 1 on the Irish Albums Chart, the UK Albums Chart, the U.S. Billboard 200 chart, and the Canadian Albums Chart. It won Album of the Year at the 2011 Grammy Awards, Best International Album at the 2011 BRIT Awards, Album of the Year at the 2011 Juno Awards, and the 2011 Polaris Music .

podcast.body: Released on August 2nd, 2010, this album is a semi-autobiographical and semi-apocalyptic exploration of the gated, planned community north of Houston, Woodlands, Texas, where Win and William Butler grew up. Recording took place in three locations: Win and Regine Butler's house in Montreal, a church they had purchased in Farnham, Quebec, and in New York. The album debuted at number one in Canada, the US, the UK, Ireland, Norway, Portugal, and Belgium, and reached the top 10 in Australia, Denmark, Germany, Mexico, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Finland, and New Zealand. It achieved platinum status in Canada and the UK, and gold in the US. This album made history by winning Album of the Year at the Grammy Awards, Juno Awards, Brit Awards (Best International Album), and the Polaris Music Prize, making it the first album to achieve such a comprehensive sweep of major awards. "The Suburbs probably sold a little more than that."

podcast.body: This album featured two distinct covers and also included a tape, showcasing a continued evolution in their physical album presentation. It is the final album in their "sacred trilogy" of early works, solidifying their status as modern classics and marking a peak in alternative music at the start of the 21st century. Markus Dravs was one of the producers who worked with the band on this album. "el de Subur que tenías a las dos portadas y cinta."

podcast.body: This album surprisingly won the Album of the Year award at the 53rd annual Grammy Awards on February 13, 2011, presented by Barbara Streisand. Its win caused a significant public reaction, with many expressing confusion and outrage on social media due to the band's relative unfamiliarity to a mainstream audience, leading to an explosion on Twitter. "And the Grammy goes to The Suburbs, Archie Pires."
